name: Παραλία Γλυφάδας Ακτή Γ
evidence: Glyfada's organized Asteras/Akti beaches are described as sandy ('unique sandy beach with turquoise waters'), though the far-north edge is slightly pebbly; disambiguated to the Glyfada Riviera coast (37.86N).

name: Νησίδα Φλέβες
evidence: 'Paralia Fleves is covered with sand and rocks' on this rocky uninhabited islet off Vouliagmeni; the ~40m beach pocket itself is sandy (rocks form the surrounding shore), so sand is the beach material.

name: Άλιμος Λουτρά
evidence: Alimos (Loutra) organized Athens-Riviera beach is 'covered with white sand and fine pebbles'; predominantly white sand; disambiguated to the Loutra tram-stop beach in Alimos.

name: Όρμος Ληδάκι
evidence: No beach-specific source found for 'Ληδάκι' cove on the Nea Makri/Rafina coast (38.03N); neighbouring coves (Ag. Andreas) are sand+fine-pebble, but the exact beach could not be pinned, so we keep our current label.

name: Πόρτο Ράφτη Αυλάκι
evidence: Avlaki (Markopoulo, blue-flag) is an organized beach 'with sand' but 'the shore is pebbly' turning sandy in the sea; sand-and-pebble mix, not pure pebbles; disambiguated to the Porto Rafti/Markopoulo Avlaki (37.87N).

name: Ωρωπός Σκάλα Ωρωπού
evidence: Skala Oropou beach is a 'soft sandy shore interspersed with pebbles... beach is pebbly, water shoes recommended, pebbles the main characteristic'; disambiguated to Skala Oropou on the North Euboean Gulf (38.32N).

name: Λουτρά
evidence: Loutra (Souvala, Aegina) is 'sandy and organized' though described as 'a small beach of coarse sand and shingle'; predominantly sand; disambiguated to Loutra Souvalas on Aegina's north coast (37.77N).

name: Αίγινα Μαραθώνας
evidence: Marathonas A/B on Aegina is a 'long sandy beach with crystal-clear shallow water', both sections sandy and family-friendly; disambiguated to Marathonas 4km from Aegina town (37.72N).

name: Παραλία Καλάμι
evidence: Kalami (Kythira) 'consists of pebbles and some sand... it has fine pebbles', a hard-to-reach cove reached from Mylopotamos; disambiguated to the center-west Kythira Kalami below Mylopotamos (36.25N).

name: Παραλία Λίμνη (Παλαιόπολη)
evidence: Limni/Paleopoli beach is 'a unique blend of crimson pebbles and pristine white sands... red and white fine pebbles'; genuine sand-and-pebble mix, not sand-only; disambiguated to the Paleopoli bay, Kythira (36.22N).

name: Φυρή Άμμος (Κάλαμος)
evidence: Fyri Ammos (Kalamos) is 'a long beach with red sand and pebbles' (blue-flag, name literally = red sand); definitely not rocks; disambiguated to the SE-Kythira Fyri Ammos near Kalamos (36.17N).

name: Παραλία Αγίου Νικολάου
evidence: North Agios Nikolaos beach on Salamina is classified 'pebble' ('a great beach with pebbles', blue-flag organized); disambiguated to the north Salamina Agios Nikolaos (37.88N).

name: Μικρή Ζωγεριά
evidence: The small/secluded Zogeria cove has 'a mixture of sand, dirt, and pebbles where the water breaks' (the large cove is coarse sand); disambiguated to Mikri Zogeria on Spetses' north side (37.28N).

name: Παραλία Πόρτο Γερμενό
evidence: Porto Germeno is 'a pebble beach... covered in small beige pebbles, the seabed very fine pebbles', split into three beaches of sand-and-small-pebble mix but pebble-dominant; disambiguated to Porto Germeno, Gulf of Corinth (38.15N).

name: Παραλία Πολιτικών
evidence: Politika beach is 'covered in fine pebbles mixed with dark sand... dark sand punctuated by white and gray pebbles'; genuine sand-and-pebble mix; disambiguated to Politika, central Evia N-Euboean Gulf (38.77N).

name: Σχοινοδαύλεια
evidence: Schinodavlia (aka Agios Dimitrios) is 'listed among the sandy beaches of Karystos' with shallow warm clean water; disambiguated to the south-Evia/Karystos gorge beach (38.14N).

name: Παραλία Χιλιαδού
evidence: Chiliadou (Fokida/Dorida, near Nafpaktos) is 'a very beautiful beach with pebble outside and sand in the sea' - the walking shore is pebble; disambiguated to the Fokida Chiliadou 7km from Nafpaktos (38.39N), not the Evia one.

name: Diaporti
evidence: Diaporti (Vourvourou, Sithonia) mostly described as 'gravel and pebbles with a pebbled sea bottom... a pebble/stone beach not really suitable for lying down' (one outlier says fine white sand); disambiguated to Diaporti by the Pounta islet, Sithonia (40.01N).

name: Παραλία Πύργου
evidence: Pirgos beach (Halkidiki) is 'a secluded, pebbly beach with a few farmhouses among plane trees and fishing boats' per Visit Halkidiki; disambiguated to Pyrgos near Metamorfosi/Nikiti on the Toroneos gulf neck (40.25N).

name: Αμμουλιανή
evidence: Ammouliani island beaches (Alykes, Megali Ammos, Karagatsia) are 'white/golden sand with crystal-clear shallow water'; disambiguated to Ammouliani island off the Athos gulf (40.33N).

name: Άργιλος
evidence: Argilos is a clay/sand beach type (named for the argilos-clay used for natural spa); Greek guides describe it as an ammoudia, not pebble/rock. Locality note: the well-documented Argilos-with-clay is the East-Crete/Xerokampos one; the Chania/SW-coast beach at these coords is same clay-sand class. Our label (άμμος) and OSM (SAND) agree.

name: Κυανή Ακτή
evidence: Grecorama/Terrabook: Kiani Akti at Kalyves/Souda (Apokoronas, Chania, 17km E of Chania) is a large sandy beach with fine sand (ψιλή άμμος) and shallow water. Coords match Kalyves. Both our label (βράχια) and OSM (ROCKS) are wrong; our own ourTypes [fine_sand,coarse_sand] were actually correct.

name: Παραλία Κουταλάς
evidence: Discover Crete / Vamos Village: Koutalas at Kokkino Chorio (Cape Drapano, Apokoronas, ~27km E of Chania) 'έχει βότσαλα και μεγάλες πέτρες' with a rocky seabed and a small sand strip. Coords match. Predominant surface is pebbles/large stones — not the ROCKS both our label (βράχια) and OSM claim.

name: Γούβες
evidence: cretanbeaches/okaycrete: Kato Gouves (18km E of Heraklion) has fine sand (λεπτή άμμος) and shallow water. Coords match Gouves. Both our label (βότσαλα) and OSM (PEBBLES) are wrong; ourTypes [fine_sand] was correct.

name: Σταλίδα
evidence: explorecrete/cretanbeaches: Stalida (Stalis, near Malia, Heraklion) is a ~3km organized beach of fine sand (ψιλή άμμος) with shallow water. Coords match. Both our label (βότσαλα) and OSM (PEBBLES) are wrong; ourTypes [fine_sand] was correct.

name: Λίμνη
evidence: cretanbeaches: the Skaleta/Sfakaki coast (Almyros gulf, ~12km NE of Rethymno) at these coords is golden fine sand (χρυσή ψιλή άμμος), a Caretta nesting shore. Disambiguated to the Rethymno gulf (lng 24.688 is E of Rethymno town, not Georgioupoli). Our label (άμμος) and OSM (SAND) agree.

name: Παραλία Ανατολικά
evidence: cretanbeaches/originalcrete: these coords (35.148/24.500) are the Agios Pavlos–Akoumiani Gialia dune coast of S Rethymno (Ammolofoi/Alatsogkremnoi), described as expansive αμμουδιά with sand dunes. Disambiguated to Agios Pavlos (Sachtouria), not Plakias. Our label (άμμος) and OSM (SAND) agree.

name: Παραλία Κεφάλα
evidence: cretanbeaches/originalcrete: Kefala is the NW end of the Akoumiani Gialia / Agios Pavlos sandy-dune stretch (S Rethymno), a sandy shore (with some scattered pebbles near the Agios Pavlos hamlet). Coords ~1km from id 690, same dune system. Our label (άμμος) and OSM (SAND) agree.

name: Σκίνος
evidence: cretanbeaches: Skinos, the second beach of Plakias (Sellia, W of the fishing shelter), 'has sand and many small rocks/stones, ideal for snorkeling; organized near the village, rockier to the west.' Sand base with pebbles/small rocks = mixed, not the pure PEBBLES our label (βότσαλα) and OSM state.

name: Άμμος Ξερόκαμπου
evidence: cretanbeaches/originalcrete: this is the sandy sector of Xerokampos (Siteia, Lasithi) — the name itself is 'Ammos' (sand) and the main beaches here (Mazida Ammos) are white/golden sand. Both our label (βότσαλα) and OSM (PEBBLES) wrong; ourTypes [fine_sand] correct.

name: Ποταμός Ξερόκαμπου
evidence: cretanbeaches: the 'Potamos' beach at the mouth of the Katsounaki gorge (Xerokampos, Siteia) is a beach 'με μεγάλα βότσαλα' (large pebbles) with a rocky seabed, not family-friendly. Coords match. Our label (βότσαλα) and OSM (PEBBLES) agree; ourTypes [fine_sand] was the outlier.

name: Μικρή παραλία
evidence: hotelpotos/afrodite-studios: ~150m from the central Pefkari beach (S Thasos, near Potos) there is 'a second, pebbly and completely unorganized beach' — the small beach at these coords. Our label (βότσαλα) and OSM (PEBBLES) agree; ourTypes [fine_sand] was the outlier.

name: Πευκάρι
evidence: thassos-view/tripadvisor: Pefkari (S Thasos) 'combines soft sand with small pebbles' — sand is the main surface with pebbles/small rocks at the edges (aqua shoes advised). Coords match. Genuinely mixed, not the pure PEBBLES our label (βότσαλα) and OSM claim.

name: Καρνάγιο
evidence: thassos-view/karnagiothassos: Karnagio at the end of Thasos-town (Limenas) old harbour sits 'at the edge of the last rock' — a rocky swim spot/beach bar, not sandy. Coords match Limenas. Both our label (άμμος) and OSM (SAND) wrong; ourTypes [rocks,pebbles] closer.

name: Κλίσμα
evidence: Greeka: Klisma (near Skala Kalirachi, W coast Thasos, 22km SW of Limenas) is 'a beautiful pebbled beach... covered with large smooth pebbles' (aqua shoes recommended). Coords match. Our label (βότσαλα) and OSM (PEBBLES) agree; ourTypes [fine_sand] was the outlier.

name: Σκάλα Πρίνου
evidence: thassos-view/go-thassos: Skala Prinou (Dasyllion, N Thasos, 15km from port) is a white/fine sandy beach (blue flag), shallow and waveless. Coords match. Both our label (βότσαλα) and OSM (PEBBLES) wrong; ourTypes [fine_sand] correct.

name: Δεή πλους
evidence: Name is garbled/untraceable; coords sit in the Plataria bay (Thesprotia) where the 1.5km main beach is golden sand but nearby coves (Gata/Kalami) are coarse/fine pebbles. Could not pin this exact spot to one source, so retain our label; our label (βότσαλα) and OSM (PEBBLES) already agree.

name: Γουβιά
evidence: discover-corfu: Gouvia Beach (sheltered bay, 8km N of Corfu Town) is 'mostly small pebbles and shingle, with some patches of coarse sand... not a fine sand beach.' Coords match. Our label (βότσαλα) and OSM (PEBBLES) agree.

name: Αρκουδάκι
evidence: paxosinfo/greekvillaholidays: Arkoudaki (N Paxos, near Lakka) is a pebble beach with a tented area by flat rocks for sunbathing; the swimmable beach surface is pebbles (some call it 'rocky' for the flanking flat rocks). Coords match. Our label (βότσαλα) and OSM (PEBBLES) agree.

name: Δεύτερη Σπιάντζα
evidence: cycladia/sandee: the Paxos 'spiantzes' near Gaios are small pebbly beaches enclosed by low rocky cliffs; Spiantza is 'a small pebbly beach' with translucent water. Coords match (SE of Gaios). Our label (βότσαλα) and OSM (PEBBLES) agree.

name: Αγία Τριάδα
evidence: Agia Triada is the port/settlement area of Othonoi (Ammos village, with Ammos Hotel + 'Ammos Beach Bar Agia Triada'); the island's main port beach 'consists of fine sand mixed with white pebbles'. Disambiguated to Othonoi (not the Corfu-Palaiokastritsa or Thessaloniki Agia Triada) via lat/lng 39.84/19.41.

name: Αγία Παρασκευή
evidence: Kefalonia's Agia Paraskevi between Sami and Agia Efimia is a pebbly beach ('white pebbles and blue waters, descend a few steps'). Disambiguated to Kefalonia (not the Thesprotia/Perdika beach of the same name) via coords near Sami 38.28/20.62.

name: Παραλία Κόλπος Κορμοράνων
evidence: Kormoranon (Cormorant Bay) is 'a beautiful secluded pebbly cove' on the Fanari-to-Argostoli coastal road near Lassi; matches lat/lng 38.19/20.47. Our label (βότσαλα) and OSM (PEBBLES) both correct.

name: Πλατιά Άμμος
evidence: Platia Ammos (Paliki peninsula, ~400 steps down) 'shore is carpeted with fine white pebbles, though some areas have pebbles so small they create the impression of a sandy beach'. Name means 'wide sand' but it is pebble. Coords 38.22/20.35 = Paliki west coast.

name: Φανάρι
evidence: Fanari on Meganisi is 'characterized by fine white pebbles... has the finest pebbles of all the beaches on the island'. Disambiguated to Meganisi via coords 38.67/20.81 (cape Atherino).

name: Μεγάλη Μυζήθρα
evidence: Greek Wikipedia/guides: the Megali Myzithra beach strip below the white conical Myzithres rocks is 'κυρίως καλυμμένη με βότσαλα' (mostly covered with pebbles), boat-access only. Coords 37.65/20.82 = SW Zakynthos cliffs.

name: Ναγός
evidence: Chios Travel Guide (Nagos, NE Chios near Kardamyla): 'αποτελείται από μικρά βότσαλα ενώ στο εσωτερικό έχει χοντρή άμμο' (small pebbles with coarse sand in the inner part). Coords 38.56/26.08 = NE Chios.

name: Παραλία Μυρσινίδι
evidence: Chios.gr (Mersinidi, Vrontados near the monastery): two beaches N and S of the church, 'αποτελούνται από άμμο και βότσαλο' (sand and pebbles), unorganized with natural shade. Coords 38.43/26.14 = Vrontados.

name: Σαλάγωνα
evidence: Chios.gr (Salagona, SW Chios ~6km from Pyrgi): 'a quiet, relatively isolated beach with coarse sand and fine pebbles'. Coords 38.22/25.91 = SW Chios (not the Karfas fine-sand beach).

name: Παραλία Ξυλοσύρτη
evidence: Xylosyrtis (S Ikaria, S of Agios Kirykos): 'a peaceful, long, pebble beach... white beach with glittering pebbles'. Described as pebble-rock but predominantly pebbles. Coords 37.59/26.25 = Xylosyrtis village. Our label βράχια and OSM ROCKS both overstate the rock.

name: Γκλιάτη
evidence: Gliati at Palaia/Ancient Epidavros: 'about 500m long, with sand and fine pebbles and clean blue waters' (sunken Roman ruins offshore). Coords 37.63/23.16 = Palaia Epidavros, not Porto Heli.

name: Παραλία Αρβανιτιά
evidence: Arvanitia, the town beach of Nafplio below Palamidi, is 'made up of white pebbles and rocks... umbrellas on the pebbles, becomes rocky at its edges'. Coords 37.56/22.80 = Nafplio.

name: Παραλία Ασίνης
evidence: Ancient Asini beach near Tolo: 'small and large pebbles on the shore... pebbles and sand, with rocky areas on the right side' (Plaka/larger Asini offers sand, fine and coarse pebbles). Coords 37.53/22.88 = Asini/Tolo. Leans pebble-dominant.

name: Κανταρέ
evidence: Kantare (west of Corinth, before Lechaio) is consistently described as 'a sandy beach with shallow waters, perfect for families' across multiple Corinthia guides. Coords 37.93/22.90 = near Lechaio. Both our label (βότσαλα) and OSM (PEBBLES) appear wrong.

name: Παραλία Αγία Σωτήρα
evidence: Agia Sotira (Loutraki-Perachora-Agioi Theodoroi coast): 'the coastline is covered with fine pebbles, while in the eastern section the beach has more rocks'. Coords 38.05/23.03 = near Agioi Theodoroi.

name: Παραλία Λυκοποριάς
evidence: Lykoporia (Xylokastro-Evrostini coast) is described with 'γαλαζοπράσινα νερά και αμμουδερό βυθό' (sandy seabed) and grouped among the area's sandy beaches ('αμμουδιές'); no source specifies pebble shore. Coords 38.14/22.49. Weakly corroborates our label; kept.

name: Παραλία Σκαλωσιά
evidence: Skalosia (Loutraki, below Geraneia mtns): 'this beach with its large white pebbles and deep turquoise waters', access via stairs of sea-stones to 'the pebble beach'. Coords 38.07/22.94.

name: Βορδόνας
evidence: Greeka (Vordonas, ~15km from Gythio near Skoutari, East Mani): 'a mostly sandy coastline, except for some rocks... rocky seafloor; predominantly sandy'. Coords 36.66/22.50. Our label and OSM (both SAND) correct.

name: Λιμάνι
evidence: Generic beach name 'Λιμάνι' (harbor) at coords 36.75/22.80 (Laconian Gulf, roughly between Skala and Asopos) could not be pinned to any beach-specific source without name collision (many 'Λιμάνι/Λιμένι' beaches in Lakonia). Keeping our current label (άμμος).

name: Χαρακιά
evidence: Charakia in Xylis bay (S of Plytra, NW coast of Archangelos bay): 'a sandy beach of 3.5km... golden sand, deep turquoise waters, and colorful pebbles where the waves break', some rocks in the water. Coords 36.66/22.88 confirm Plytra/Archangelos (not the East-Mani Kotronas 'Charakia'). Predominantly sand; our label and OSM (SAND) correct.

name: Μεγάλο Μαράθι
evidence: Messinia guides (Pylos, between Finikounda-Koroni) repeatedly call Mikro/Megalo Marathi 'two wonderful sandy beaches (αμμώδεις)'; disambiguated by Pylos/Tsapi dirt-road access matching lat/lng.

name: Μικρό Μαράθι
evidence: Same Messinia cove pair as Megalo Marathi: 'The beaches are sandy... two wonderful sandy beaches, small and large Marathi'; Pylos.info/pylos-area sources confirm.

name: Άγιος Παύλος
evidence: Amorgos guides: 'tongue of fine white pebbles' with 'a strip of sand extending into the sea', opposite Nikouria islet (matches lat/lng) - sand-and-pebble, not rock.

name: Καμπί
evidence: Amorgos (near Hozoviotissa/Agia Anna, matches lat/lng): 'coarse and fine pebbles', a small pebbled nudist cove - pebbles, not rock.

name: Foniadiko
evidence: Remote Ios beach ('Φοντάδικο', reached by dirt road branching toward Agia Theodoti) with no published composition data found; kept our label (ours and OSM both say sand).

name: Σαρακήνικο
evidence: Milos Sarakiniko (north coast, ~5km from Plaka, matches lat/lng): Wikipedia describes it as 'a narrow strip of sand between all-white volcanic rocks' - beach surface is sand though famed for surrounding white rock slabs.

name: Βούδια
evidence: Milos Voudia (near Pollonia, pink volcanic cliffs, matches lat/lng): 'pebbles beach... white pebble and pink sand', clear stones of various sizes mixed with light sand - mixed, leans pebbles, not pure sand.

name: Βίντζι
evidence: Naxos Chora, below Portara (matches lat/lng): the smaller Chora beach, 'small stretch of sand', a man-made sandy beach for a quick swim - sand, not rock (distinct from rocky Grotta next door).

name: Γρόττα
evidence: Naxos Chora north seaside (matches lat/lng): 'very rocky... a small bay strewn with a mixture of pebbles and some sand', for snorkeling rather than swimming - predominantly rock/pebble.

name: Δρυός
evidence: Paros SE coast settlement Dryos (matches lat/lng): 'the beach of Dryos consists of sand and pebbles' - mixed, not pure pebbles.

name: Αμπέλα
evidence: Syros SW near Megas Gialos (matches lat/lng): Greeka 'a small, sandy shore with some scattered pebbles... soft sand' - predominantly sand, not pebbles.

name: Παραλία Λωτό
evidence: Syros western coast Lotos (matches lat/lng): 'partly organized seashore with sand and pebbles... soft sand and pebbles around the shore' - mixed, not pure pebbles.

name: Κασόνια
evidence: Kalymnos town beach (Kasonia, closest to Pothia, matches lat/lng): 'a long sandy beach... strewn with sand and pebbles', with tamarisk trees - predominantly sand, not pebbles.

name: Ποτάλι
evidence: Karpathos west coast near Kato Lefkos (matches lat/lng): 'characterized by gray pebbles and coarse sand in some places', with some rocks at the sides in the sea - pebble/coarse-sand, not primarily rock.

name: Θερμά
evidence: Kos SE hot-springs beach (Embros Thermae after Agios Fokas, matches lat/lng): 'mostly covered with dark sand and stones... dark pebbles' from volcanic activity - mixed dark sand and pebbles/stones, not pure sand.

name: Κισσίρια
evidence: Obscure northern Lipsi beach (listed by name in the municipality/CityMobile catalog but with no composition description); no reliable surface source found, kept our label.

name: Κοίμηση
evidence: Lipsi, below the Church of Koimisis (SW/NW, reached via carved path, matches lat/lng): 'characterized by pebbles... pebble and gravel' - pebbles, not sand.

name: Κορακιά
evidence: Obscure eastern Lipsi cove not featured in any beach guide (Korakia hits return other regions - Lavreotiki/Crete); could not pin the Lipsi one, kept our label.

name: Πνιγμένος
evidence: Obscure Lipsi cove absent from all beach listings/guides; no composition source found, kept our label.

name: Στίφη
evidence: Obscure Lipsi cove absent from all beach listings/guides; no composition source found, kept our label.

name: Παραλία Καλλιθέας (Oasis)
evidence: Rhodes Kallithea/Oasis (lat 36.375, coast S of Rhodes town): sources state 'Oasis Beach features a rocky beach rather than sandy' with sculpted rocks and micro-coves; matches our βράχια and OSM ROCKS.

name: Παραλία Φούρνοι
evidence: Fourni below Monolithos, SW Rhodes (lat 36.106): 'covered with golden brown sand which turns a bit stony near the water, a significant portion is pebbled, but sandy patches can also be found' — sand+pebble mix, not pure sand as our label and OSM claim.

name: Σύμη Γυάλα
evidence: Symi (lat 36.62): island beaches 'almost all have pebbles and little or no sand'; consistent with our βότσαλα and OSM PEBBLES for this Symi cove.

name: ΠΔΕ Καστελόκαμπος
evidence: Kastelokampos by the Rio bridge, Achaia (lat 38.29, lng 21.77): 'a mix of golden sand and pebbles ... continuous strip of sand and pebbles ~1.2km' — mixed, not the pebbles-only of our label and OSM.

name: Kitesurf Spot
evidence: Kite spot on the SE coastal section of Nafpaktos near Grimbovo (lat 38.38, lng 21.85); the Nafpaktos shoreline here is fine-pebble/gravel, matching our βότσαλα and OSM PEBBLES.

name: Ασπρογιάλι
evidence: Asprogiali 7km from Astakos toward Vonitsa (lat 38.54, lng 21.01): 'Η παραλία είναι βοτσαλωτή' (pebbly) — contradicts our άμμος and OSM SAND.

name: Γρίμποβο
evidence: Gribovo in Nafpaktos (lat 38.39, lng 21.835): 'coarse sand and pebbles, with velvety sand ... pebbles dotting the water's edge' — mixed, not pebbles-only as our label/OSM say.

name: Παραλία Κανάλι
evidence: Coords (lat 38.44, lng 21.35) sit in the Kryoneri/Kato Vasiliki stretch of Nafpaktia (Kryoneri = 'fine-pebbled and sandy'), but no source specifically identifies a beach named 'Κανάλι' here to confirm composition; keep current label.

name: Παραλία Κουλούρι
evidence: Koulouri at Sparto on the Ambrakian Gulf, Amfilochia (lat 38.91, lng 21.11) is confirmed as an existing swimming beach, but no source states its sand/pebble composition; keep current άμμος label.

name: Παραλία Ρούγας
evidence: Rouga cove near Paliambela on the S Ambrakian Gulf (lat 38.92, lng 21.00): 'a pebbly beach and deeply shaded trees' — contradicts our άμμος and OSM SAND.

name: Πλαζ Ναυπάκτου
evidence: Psani plage W of Nafpaktos harbor (lat 38.39, lng 21.827): 'continuous strip of fine pebbles extends ~1.7km ... also has sandy areas' — fine-pebble predominant, matching our βότσαλα and OSM PEBBLES (some sand present).

name: Αλόννησος Μηλιά
evidence: Milia (not Chrysi Milia) on Alonissos (lat 39.16): 'there are large pebbles at first, while deeper into the water there is sand' — pebble shore, matching our βότσαλα and OSM PEBBLES.

name: Ξάνεμο
evidence: Xanemos by Skiathos airport (lat 39.19, lng 23.51): 'coarse grey sand mixed with pebbles ... a line of shingle around the water's edge' — mixed, not pure sand as our label and OSM claim.

name: Άγιος Ιωάννης
evidence: Agios Ioannis Kastri (Mamma Mia chapel), NW Skopelos (lat 39.17, lng 23.65): 'a narrow pebble beach ... combination of sand, pebbles and small rocks' — predominantly pebble/rock, not sand as our label and OSM claim.

name: Στάφυλος
evidence: Stafylos, 4km S of Skopelos town (lat 39.09, lng 23.75): 'mixed pebbles with fine gray sand ... a delightful mix of golden sand and smooth pebbles' — sand+pebble mix, not pebbles-only as our label/OSM say.

name: Άγιος Ιωάννης
evidence: Agios Ioannis, Pelion/Zagora (lat 39.417, lng 23.16): 'built on a unique sandy area with white pearl-like pebbles', longest organized beach in Magnesia — sand+pebble, definitely not the βράχια/ROCKS our label and OSM claim.

name: Άγιος Ιωάννης (Ζαγορά)
evidence: Same beach as id 2670 (lat 39.418, lng 23.16), Agios Ioannis Pelion: 'sandy area with white pearl-like pebbles' — sand+pebble, not βράχια/ROCKS as our label and OSM claim.

name: Αγιά Θυμιά
evidence: Agia Thymia, S Pelion Pagasitic coast near Afissos/Lefokastro (lat 39.26, lng 23.18): 'a spacious pebbly cove, wild, with no amenities' (sandy seafloor) — pebble surface, not sand as our label and OSM claim.
